html:
Kerak is a huge Crusader castle on a ridge east of the Dead Sea in Jordan, begun in 1142 to guard the road between Damascus and Egypt and the pilgrim route to Mecca.

Its most famous lord, Raynald of Châtillon, raided the caravans and even sent ships into the Red Sea toward Mecca. Saladin besieged the castle in 1183 and 1184 without success. After his victory at the Battle of Hattin in 1187 he executed Raynald, and Kerak surrendered after a long siege.

The Mamluks later rebuilt and strengthened it. It still dominates the town of Kerak and is one of the largest castles of the Crusader states.
sum: Kerak is a huge Crusader castle on a ridge east of the Dead Sea in Jordan, begun in 1142 to guard the road between Damascus and Egypt and the pilgrim route to Mecca.
